chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Mis'mam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who forgot to throw the pebbles on the second day, so he started with Jamarat al-Aqabah, then al-Wusta, then al-Ula, he said: 'He delays what he threw, so he throws the middle Jamarah, then Jamarat al-Aqabah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgot to throw pebbles on the second day of Hajj?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the validity of the missed ritual depends on restoring the original chronological sequence (middle then Aqabah) rather than the order of actual performance, ensuring the pilgrim rectifies the specific omission. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the structural integrity of Hajj pillars even when errors occur, distinguishing it from mere corrective compensation. The principle underscores the importance of intentionality and order in ritual acts, a key theme in Usul al-Fiqh regarding *nasi* (forgetfulness).
